title: Burning ropes
prompt: You have two ropes. Each takes exactly 60 minutes to burn from one end to the other. However, the ropes are not uniform — they burn at different rates along their length. You cannot use remaining rope length to estimate time.
You have matches. You may light either end of either rope at any moment.
What is the correct first action to measure exactly 45 minutes?
answer: light both ends of rope 1 and one end of rope 2
answer_display: Light both ends of rope 1 and one end of rope 2
hints: If you light both ends of a rope simultaneously, how long does it take to finish burning — regardless of how non-uniform it is?
Once rope 1 is gone, 30 minutes have passed. Rope 2 has 30 minutes of burn time left from one end. How do you make it burn twice as fast?
Light the second end of rope 2 the moment rope 1 burns out. It will exhaust itself in exactly 15 more minutes.
solution_lede:
The key insight: lighting both ends of a rope simultaneously halves its total burn time, regardless of how non-uniform the rope is. A 60-minute rope lit at both ends burns out in exactly 30 minutes.

So: at t=0, light both ends of rope 1 and one end of rope 2 simultaneously. Rope 1 burns out at t=30 minutes. At that exact moment, light the second end of rope 2. Rope 2 had 30 minutes of burn time remaining from one end — with both ends now burning, it takes exactly 15 more minutes.

30 + 15 = 45 minutes.

solution_steps.body: t=0: Light both ends of rope 1, and one end of rope 2.
t=30 min: Rope 1 burns out. Rope 2 has exactly 30 minutes of burn time remaining from one end.
Immediately light the other end of rope 2. With both ends burning, it will exhaust in exactly 15 minutes.
t=45 min: Rope 2 burns out. Exactly 45 minutes have elapsed.

options: Light one end of each rope
Light both ends of rope 1 and one end of rope 2
Light both ends of both ropes
Light one end of rope 1 only
